colors.description: Shared colours by id, referred to from colour properties as "var(--<id>)".

additionalProperties.description: A named colour that belongs to the drawing. A stroke, a fill or a layer colour refers to it by writing "var(--<id>)" in place of a colour; changing the value here then changes everything that refers to it.

materials.description: Materials by id, referred to from walls and the floors of rooms by "material".

fill.description: The colour it is drawn in where it is cut, in a wall or a floor. A CSS colour or a shared colour reference. White when not given.

pattern.description: The pattern drawn over that colour: the hatching that tells the material.

kind.description: Which pattern: 'Lines', 'Cross', 'Planks', 'Tiles', 'Dots' or 'Zigzag'; 'None' for no pattern where one would otherwise be taken from a material.

spacing.description: Distance between its strokes, in mm. Each pattern has its own when not given.

angle.description: Degrees its strokes are turned by. Each pattern has its own when not given.

stroke.description: The colour of its strokes. A CSS colour or a shared colour reference.

strokeWidth.description: The weight of its strokes, in screen pixels as in a style. 0.6 when not given.

opacity.description: How opaque its strokes are, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (the default), on top of the opacity of their colour.

additionalProperties.description: A material the drawing is built of: concrete, brick, insulation, plaster, a floor finish. It belongs to the drawing, as a shared colour does: walls and the floors of rooms refer to it by its id, are drawn in its colour and pattern, and are counted under its name. The material of id "default" is what walls are made of until given another: walls of no material take its fill and pattern, unless they give their own; it cannot be removed.

style.description: The dimension line and its end markers, as the "style" of a dimension.

verticalText.description: Which way text along a vertical dimension line reads: 'up', from bottom to top, read with the head turned to the left or from the right-hand side of the sheet (as ISO 129 asks); 'down' (the default), from top to bottom, read with the head turned to the right. fraction.description: With unit 'ft-in': the fraction of an inch the value is rounded to, as its lower number (2, 4, 8, 16, 32). Defaults to 16.

decimal.description: The decimal separator of the value, in place of the drawing's ("settings"). Left out, the drawing's.

sheet.description: Makes the component what is on every sheet of the drawing: a title, a logo, a north arrow. It is the size, in millimetres of real paper, of the sheet its children are drawn on (297 × 210 for an A4 lying), from that sheet's top-left corner. Every paper draws them over itself at its own scale, each kept at its distance from the corner of the sheet it is nearest to, so a sheet of another size has them in its own corners. In their texts, {sheet}, {scale}, {format}, {page}, {project} and the other fields are filled in for each sheet. A drawing has one such component; a paper that is "plain" leaves it out.

oneOf.description: A room: the space enclosed by the walls and dividers around the point (x, y), which is also where its name and area are written. schedule.description: What it counts, which is worked out again each time it is drawn: 'objects' (each component and each kind of parametric object, with how many are placed), 'floors' (the floor area of each material), 'rooms' (each room and its area), 'walls' (the walls by material and thickness: how many, length, face and volume) or 'openings' (doors and windows by kind and size). An unknown one draws an empty table.

columns.description: The fields shown, in order. Left out, the schedule's usual ones. Fields: objects: symbol (each drawn as it is on the plan), name, count; floors: material, rooms, area; rooms: name, material, area; walls: material, thickness, count, length, area, volume; openings: kind, width, height, count.

labels.description: The words the table is written with, by field (the heading of its column), and 'total' (the last row) and 'none' (what stands for no material or no type). Left out, English ones.

size.description: Text size in mm. Defaults to 200.

source.description: The id of the page whose contents it counts. Defaults to the page it is on.

totals.description: Whether a last row adds up the columns that can be added up. Defaults to true.

rowsPerBlock.description: At most this many rows of things counted one under the other: the next ones go into a block beside it, with the headings again, and so on, the total at the end of the last. Left out, all in one block.

only.description: The rows shown, by their keys; the others are left out of the table and its total, and what comes on the plan later is not shown. Keys: objects 'component:<id>', or for a parametric object 'parametric:' then its kind and every one of its parameters, defaults filled in, as JSON with its keys in order ('parametric:arch.radiator {"length":800,...}': a model with other parameters is another row); floors 'material:<id>' ('material:' for the floors of no material); rooms 'room:<id>'; walls 'material:<id>' and the thickness in mm, as 'material:brick 200' ('material: 200' for the default material); openings the kind, then width and height in metres, as 'arch.door 0.9 2.1', whatever the table's units. Left out, every row.

decimal.description: The decimal separator of its numbers, in place of the drawing's "settings". Left out (as it should be), the drawing's.

system.description: 'imperial' gives lengths in feet, areas in square feet, volumes in cubic feet and thicknesses in inches, in place of the drawing's "settings". Left out (as it should be), the drawing's.

language.description: The language code its rows are named in where they take a name from an extension, as "fr".

oneOf.description: A table of quantities placed on the drawing, its top-left corner at (x, y): what is on a page, counted and measured, and kept up to date as the drawing changes.

parent.description: Id of the page, component or group this node is directly inside. Null for pages and components.

order.description: Fractional index giving the z-order among siblings (plain string comparison, later = on top). A key of the fractional-indexing package, such as "a0", "a1" or "a0V"; leave it out when adding a node to put it on top.

layer.description: Id of the layer the node is on. A node inside a component has none: what a component holds is drawn on the layer of each of its instances.

style.description: Overrides the look of a node. Unset values fall back to the node kind, then the layer color. An instance has none: it looks as its component is drawn.

stroke.description: CSS color of lines and text, or 'none'. Any colour property may instead be a shared colour, "var(--<id>)", or "var(--layer)": the colour of the node's layer.

strokeWidth.description: Line weight in screen pixels (does not scale with zoom). On paper one pixel prints as 0.25 mm, so 2 is a 0.5 mm line.

fill.description: CSS fill color, or 'none', a shared colour "var(--<id>)", or "var(--layer)" to fill with the colour of the node's layer.

kind.description: Which pattern: 'Lines', 'Cross', 'Planks', 'Tiles', 'Dots' or 'Zigzag'; 'None' for no pattern where one would otherwise be taken from a material.

spacing.description: Distance between its strokes, in mm. Each pattern has its own when not given.

angle.description: Degrees its strokes are turned by. Each pattern has its own when not given.

stroke.description: The colour of its strokes. A CSS colour or a shared colour reference.

strokeWidth.description: The weight of its strokes, in screen pixels as in a style. 0.6 when not given.

opacity.description: How opaque its strokes are, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (the default), on top of the opacity of their colour.

pattern.description: A pattern of strokes drawn over a fill, inside each closed shape: the hatching that tells a material, or a floor.

modifiers.description: Modifiers applied to what this node draws, one after the other in this order. On a group or an instance they apply to everything it holds.

type.description: The kind of modifier: 'crop', or one registered by an extension. Unknown kinds are kept and skipped.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A modifier that is switched off stays in the list.

params.description: Parameters of the kind. Missing ones use the kind defaults.

frame.description: Where the modifier sits on the drawing: positions among its parameters are relative to it. It follows the node when the node is moved, turned or scaled.

items.description: A non-destructive change to how a node is drawn; the node itself is not altered. 'crop' shows only what is inside the rectangle that starts at its frame and has params.width and params.height.

material.description: The id of the material it is made of, among the drawing's "materials": it is drawn in its colour and pattern unless its style gives its own, and counted under it. Left out, it is of the default material. Walls of one material that meet are drawn as one; between walls of different materials that touch, a line is drawn. A wall built of several materials (brick lined with insulation, then plaster) is several walls side by side, each of one.

justify.description: Which line of the wall a and b are: absent or "center", its middle; "left" or "right", that face, as the wall runs from a to b, the whole thickness then lying on the other side. Corners are where these lines meet, so walls drawn by the same face keep that face flush whatever their thicknesses, and a change of thickness grows away from the line.

bulge.description: Makes the wall curved: how far, in mm, the middle of its line (see "justify") stands off the straight line from a to b, the wall then following the arc of a circle through a, that point and b. Positive bows to the right of the direction a to b as seen on screen, negative to the left. At most half the distance from a to b, which is a half circle. Absent or 0 is a straight wall.

height.description: How high it stands, in mm, when that differs from its page. Used to measure its face; nothing is drawn with it.

edges.description: The lines of its outline one by one, each with a look of its own over the wall's style. "left" and "right" are its two faces, as it runs from a to b; "a" and "b" are the lines across its ends. "show": false hides a line. Across an end, left out, the line is drawn when the end is free or stops against another wall, and not where two walls are joined into one; "show": true draws the line between two joined walls (what cutting a wall in two gives).

strokeWidth.description: In screen pixels, as in a style.

joins.description: How each end is finished where it meets exactly one other wall. Left out (the default), the corner is automatic: a sharp point, cut off when the walls meet at less than 60° and the point would stick out. 'miter' keeps the sharp point at any angle, 'round' and 'bevel' round or cut that corner off, and 'through' with 'butt' on the other wall's end lets this wall run past while the other stops against it. Give both ends of a corner the same value, or the through/butt pair. 'free' joins this end to nothing, even where other walls end at the same point: it ends square, or cut along the side of a wall it stops against, and moving those walls leaves it where it is.

oneOf.description: A wall along the line a-b (its middle, or one of its faces with "justify"), straight or, with "bulge", an arc. Walls sharing an endpoint are drawn joined.

pattern.description: A pattern of strokes drawn over a fill, inside each closed shape: the hatching that tells a material, or a floor.

modifiers.description: Modifiers applied to what this node draws, one after the other in this order. On a group or an instance they apply to everything it holds.

type.description: The kind of modifier: 'crop', or one registered by an extension. Unknown kinds are kept and skipped.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A modifier that is switched off stays in the list.

params.description: Parameters of the kind. Missing ones use the kind defaults.

frame.description: Where the modifier sits on the drawing: positions among its parameters are relative to it. It follows the node when the node is moved, turned or scaled.

items.description: A non-destructive change to how a node is drawn; the node itself is not altered. 'crop' shows only what is inside the rectangle that starts at its frame and has params.width and params.height.

meta.description: Free-form data for extensions and tools.

offset.description: Signed distance from the measured points to the dimension line.

text.description: Replaces the measured value when set.

dimensionStyle.description: The id of the dimension style it is drawn in, among the document's "dimensionStyles". It takes what the style defines, except where it gives itself a value.

startMarker.description: Symbol at this end of the dimension line. Defaults to 'tick'.

endMarker.description: Symbol at this end of the dimension line. Defaults to 'tick'.

markerSize.description: Length of the end markers in mm. Defaults to 100.

extension.description: Look of the two extension lines. Unset values follow the dimension line.

stroke.description: CSS color of lines and text, or 'none'. Any colour property may instead be a shared colour, "var(--<id>)", or "var(--layer)": the colour of the node's layer.

strokeWidth.description: Line weight in screen pixels (does not scale with zoom). On paper one pixel prints as 0.25 mm, so 2 is a 0.5 mm line.

extensionGap.description: Gap in mm between a measured point and its extension line. Defaults to 0.

size.description: Text size in mm. Defaults to 150.

font.description: CSS font family, e.g. 'serif'. Defaults to the system sans-serif.

textColor.description: Defaults to the color of the dimension line.

textPosition.description: Where the text sits relative to the dimension line. Defaults to 'above'.

verticalText.description: Which way text along a vertical dimension line reads: 'up', from bottom to top, read with the head turned to the left or from the right-hand side of the sheet (as ISO 129 asks); 'down' (the default), from top to bottom, read with the head turned to the right. A line within a degree of vertical counts as vertical; text along any other line reads from below.

unit.description: Unit the measured value is shown in. Defaults to 'mm'. 'ft-in' writes feet and inches with a fraction, as 7' 6 1/2". Coordinates stay in mm whatever this is.

fraction.description: With unit 'ft-in': the fraction of an inch the value is rounded to, as its lower number (2, 4, 8, 16, 32). Defaults to 16.

decimals.description: Decimal places. Defaults to 0 for mm, 1 for cm and in, 2 for m and ft.

showUnit.description: Append the unit to the value.

decimal.description: The decimal separator of the value, in place of the drawing's ("settings"). Left out, the drawing's.

oneOf.description: A linear dimension: an annotation showing the distance between a and b. The node "style" styles the dimension line and its end markers.

parent.description: Id of the page, component or group this node is directly inside. Null for pages and components.

order.description: Fractional index giving the z-order among siblings (plain string comparison, later = on top). A key of the fractional-indexing package, such as "a0", "a1" or "a0V"; leave it out when adding a node to put it on top.

layer.description: Id of the layer the node is on. A node inside a component has none: what a component holds is drawn on the layer of each of its instances.

style.description: Overrides the look of a node. Unset values fall back to the node kind, then the layer color. An instance has none: it looks as its component is drawn.

fill.description: CSS fill color, or 'none', a shared colour "var(--<id>)", or "var(--layer)" to fill with the colour of the node's layer.

kind.description: Which pattern: 'Lines', 'Cross', 'Planks', 'Tiles', 'Dots' or 'Zigzag'; 'None' for no pattern where one would otherwise be taken from a material.

spacing.description: Distance between its strokes, in mm. Each pattern has its own when not given.

decimal.description: The decimal separator of the areas, tables and dimensions. Defaults to '.'.
